source_confidence: High descriptive confidence in M9A; not confirmatory.
scientific_importance: High: targets the largest recorded error and a specific calibration failure.
falsifiability: High: M9B fixes a paired slope-deficit interval and slope thresholds before C.
explanatory_discrimination: High for interference-specific attenuation versus general source bias; cannot separate training shift, capacity, target construction or features.
data_compute_requirements: Moderate: one new evaluation-only source set plus pilot; frozen-model inference only; no training.
new_cases_or_fonts: New cases and render/corruption seeds; no new fonts required.
leakage_confounding_risk: Moderate: source composition, unequal target gaps, nonlinearity and out-of-distribution training shift remain.
expected_information_gain: Highest of the three: support would justify a separate intervention-design decision; falsification would retire attenuation.
project_relevance: High: directly addresses the M8C/M9A interference error that motivates M9B.
negative_result_value: High: a clear falsification or precision failure narrows the research programme.
key_unresolved_assumptions: Linear within-source slope is adequate; C is independent and large enough; 90% source retention and precision are attainable; the M8C-derived effect generalises.
implementation_complexity: Moderate: new data generation, slope estimator, source-grouped bootstrap, one-shot analysis lock.
recommendation: Best candidate only if experimentation is separately reopened; not authorized by M9C.
rationale: Most central, most discriminative and least externally dependent; still requires new independent C and cannot support a model change.

source_confidence: Low-to-moderate exploratory; M9A associations are descriptive and not source-clustered inference.
scientific_importance: Medium: tests whether the frozen features conflate interference with benign edge/sharpness variation.
falsifiability: High in principle: matched residual interval plus balance and coverage guards; high risk of not_testable.
explanatory_discrimination: Low-to-moderate: matching can show residual excess but cannot identify a feature or prove feature inadequacy; overlap may fail.
data_compute_requirements: Moderate-to-high: C plus feature matching, target-bin overlap, caliper and standardisation; no training.
new_cases_or_fonts: New cases and seeds; no new fonts required.
leakage_confounding_risk: High: correlated features, target/severity, selection, regression to the mean, omitted texture and distribution shift.
expected_information_gain: Low-to-moderate per unit effort; support would not justify a feature change; not_testable is a likely outcome.
project_relevance: Medium: feature representation is central, but M6A-M6D found no defensible gain and M7A found severe redundancy.
negative_result_value: Moderate: would weaken conflation, but an unmatched or overlap failure is uninformative.
key_unresolved_assumptions: Adequate overlap exists; the caliper and standardisation can be frozen without C; matching identifies a meaningful excess rather than selection; the eight features are the right representation.
implementation_complexity: High: matching, balance diagnostics, deterministic tie-breaking, coverage accounting and source grouping.
recommendation: Deprioritize; do not fund before H1 and only with a new protocol if a specific feature question remains.
rationale: Low explanatory leverage, high matching risk, and existing feature studies already argue against a feature intervention.

source_confidence: Moderate descriptive confidence in M9A; font effects are entangled with target difficulty and glyph properties.
scientific_importance: Medium: tests a conditional font/glyph modifier and cross-font robustness.
falsifiability: High on paper: matched case-cluster contrast plus per-font sign checks; font availability and overlap can make it not_testable.
explanatory_discrimination: Low-to-moderate: conditional association only; cannot separate font identity, glyph shape, metrics, hinting, renderer, target construction or case composition.
data_compute_requirements: High: C and pilot plus new licensed fonts, stroke classification and new cases; no training.
new_cases_or_fonts: Yes: at least two new thin-stroke and two new thick-stroke fonts, licence-eligible and unused; also new cases and seeds.
leakage_confounding_risk: High: font identity is entangled with glyphs, metrics, hinting, rasterisation and the font-specific clean reference; fixed renderer; small purposive roster.
expected_information_gain: Low-to-moderate: a supported result is a narrow conditional contrast, not a mechanism or population claim.
project_relevance: Medium: follows M7B/M8C font differences, but those results already describe the observed roster within stated limits.
negative_result_value: Moderate: falsification constrains the font story; a licensing or overlap failure is costly and uninformative.
key_unresolved_assumptions: A licence-eligible new roster can be assembled; stroke-width classification is stable; target overlap is adequate; the fixed renderer supports a useful contrast; the roster is not a population.
implementation_complexity: Very high: external font dependency, licence audit, new roster, matching, case-cluster bootstrap.
recommendation: Deprioritize; consider only after a separate font-licensing and roster decision and never as a model-change justification.
rationale: Highest external dependency and weakest causal identification; not the best use of remaining project effort.
